items.text: Process tree is correct: explorer.exe (no process-create event) → control.exe → rundll32.exe (System32) → rundll32.exe (SysWOW64) → wscript.exe

Explained that a .cpl is a DLL run through control.exe and rundll32 Control_RunDLL, and that the second, 32-bit rundll32 (shell32 #44) is Windows' normal handling of a 32-bit applet, not a separate attack stage
Identified wscript.exe running info.txt with /e:JScript.Encode as an encoded script disguised with a .txt extension
Noticed wscript's CommandLine says System32 but its Image is SysWOW64, and explained it as WOW64 redirection rather than spoofing
Used the PCA Event ID 17 at 21:11:17 to corroborate the .cpl ran, and treated the procexp64.exe PCA events as unrelated or unexplained, not attacker activity
Noticed the .cpl's CreationUtcTime (21:09:48) is earlier than the write (21:11:11), without claiming to know how the file arrived
Noticed Sysmon record 4862 is missing and concluded the export is partial
Listed at least three things the logs can't tell you (e.g. how the .cpl arrived, who wrote info.txt, what wscript did next)
Classified it as a true positive and recommended isolating the host and collecting the .cpl and info.txt
